title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Amid a fragile ceasefire in effect since April 8 following intense US-Iran hostilities, Tehran is reviewing Washington's latest peace proposal as of May 7, which sources say would formally end the war while deferring issues like the Strait of Hormuz access, nuclear program curbs, and sanctions relief. President Trump, signaling "very good talks" yet warning of escalation—including strikes on Iranian assets yesterday—issued a one-week deadline for Iran's response, underscoring high-stakes bilateral negotiations mediated by Pakistan. Traders price a year-end permanent deal as the frontrunner at around 70% implied probability, reflecting optimism from proposal exchanges but uncertainty over sticking points like ballistic missiles and regional proxies, with Iran's reply expected imminently potentially shifting odds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Oklahoma City Thunder lead 1-0 in their Western Conference semifinals series against the Los Angeles Lakers after a dominant 108-90 Game 1 win at home, fueled by Chet Holmgren's 24 points and 12 rebounds despite Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's off night. Game 2 remains at OKC, amplifying the Thunder's home-court advantage and their perfect 4-0 regular-season sweep of the Lakers, backed by the NBA's best 64-18 record. Key injuries shape the matchup: Lakers rule out Luka Doncic (hamstring strain) and Jarred Vanderbilt (finger dislocation from Game 1), while Thunder miss Jalen Williams (hamstring); Luke Kennard is available despite neck soreness. LeBron James and OKC's depth will test Lakers' resilience amid back-to-back road pressure.

This overwhelming mandate positions Magyar for formal election as prime minister by early May, with the inaugural parliamentary session required by May 12; recent cabinet announcements, including Hungary's first blind minister, and diplomatic outreach to leaders like Italy's Giorgia Meloni underscore the smooth transition. Trader consensus at 99.9% reflects this constitutional inevitability under Hungary's electoral system, where the largest party forms government. Challenges would require extraordinary disruptions, such as presidential refusal to convene parliament or legal injunctions, both highly improbable given Tisza's majority.

title: Iran closes its airspace by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran initiates a major closure of its airspace, that is not solely due to weather conditions, by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or suspension of commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from Iranian airspace or a major Iranian Airspace region. A qualifying closure must apply generally to flights across Iran or a major Iranian airspace region. Limited cancellations, delays, or other partial closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain flights pre-approved by the Iranian Civil Aviation Authority may be permitted). 

Any non-weather complete suspension of commercial arrivals and departures affecting at least two of the following airports will qualify: Imam Khomeini International Airport (IKA), Mehrabad Airport (THR), Mashhad International Airport (MHD), Shiraz International Airport (SYZ), or Isfahan International Airport (IFN).

Qualifying previous examples include the January 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace except to international flights with express governmental permission (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shuts-airspace-most-flights-flightradar24-says-2026-01-14/) and the April 2024 closure of Iran’s western airspace (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-airports-cancel-flights-until-monday-morning-2024-04-14/). Non-qualifying examples include the January 27, 2026 partial closure of Iranian airspace around the Strait of Hormuz (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-issues-airspace-notice-for-military-drills-near-strait-of-hormuz/3812508) and the January 25 - April 25, 2026 VFR (Visual Flight Rules) flights suspension which did not broadly close commercial aviation in a qualifying region (https://www.intellinews.com/iran-suspends-general-aviation-and-vfr-flights-in-new-airspace-directive-421997/).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Iran will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Iranian aviation authorities and a consensus of credible reporting.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran initiates a major closure of its airspace, that is not solely due to weather conditions, by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or suspension of commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from Iranian airspace or a major Iranian Airspace region. A qualifying closure must apply generally to flights across Iran or a major Iranian airspace region. Limited cancellations, delays, or other partial closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain flights pre-approved by the Iranian Civil Aviation Authority may be permitted). 

Any non-weather complete suspension of commercial arrivals and departures affecting at least two of the following airports will qualify: Imam Khomeini International Airport (IKA), Mehrabad Airport (THR), Mashhad International Airport (MHD), Shiraz International Airport (SYZ), or Isfahan International Airport (IFN).

Qualifying previous examples include the January 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace except to international flights with express governmental permission (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shuts-airspace-most-flights-flightradar24-says-2026-01-14/) and the April 2024 closure of Iran’s western airspace (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-airports-cancel-flights-until-monday-morning-2024-04-14/). Non-qualifying examples include the January 27, 2026 partial closure of Iranian airspace around the Strait of Hormuz (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-issues-airspace-notice-for-military-drills-near-strait-of-hormuz/3812508) and the January 25 - April 25, 2026 VFR (Visual Flight Rules) flights suspension which did not broadly close commercial aviation in a qualifying region (https://www.intellinews.com/iran-suspends-general-aviation-and-vfr-flights-in-new-airspace-directive-421997/).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Iran will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Iranian aviation authorities and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Iran's Civil Aviation Authority partially reopened eastern airspace and key airports like Mashhad and Imam Khomeini on April 18-21 after nearly two months of broad closures triggered by US-Israeli strikes beginning February 28, reflecting de-escalation under a fragile April 8 ceasefire mediated by Pakistan. This shift drives trader consensus toward low near-term probabilities for a qualifying major closure—affecting at least two major airports beyond limited exceptions or weather. Persistent risks linger from May 7 Iranian claims of downing a US drone over the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi restrictions on US military airspace access. Upcoming Trump-Xi summit and China-brokered talks could stabilize tensions, though ceasefire violations by Israel in Lebanon or IRGC responses remain key escalation triggers.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President JD Vance holds a slim edge in trader consensus for the 2028 presidential election at 19.6%, trailed closely by California Governor Gavin Newsom (16.7%) and Secretary of State Marco Rubio (14.8%), reflecting a fragmented early field ahead of 2026 midterms and primaries. Recent GOP primary polls, including CPAC's March straw poll (Vance 53%, Rubio 35%) and a February New Hampshire survey showing Vance's dominance among Republicans, bolster his lead as the incumbent administration's heir apparent, while Rubio has surged on foreign policy achievements like Venezuela developments. Democrats remain scattered post-2024, with Newsom gaining in youth polls amid Harris's low standing. The race stays tight due to untested national appeal and pending midterm results in swing states; separation could emerge from Trump endorsements, administration performance on economy and immigration, or early primary polling shifts.
